claims.statement: Verified fact: the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026; importers above the 50-tonne threshold in covered sectors must become authorized declarants, buy certificates, declare embedded emissions, and surrender corresponding certificates.
Verified fact: CBAM verification operates at the non-EU installation level and accredited verifiers provide reasonable assurance over embedded-emissions calculations.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): importers will pay for an internal forecast-to-actual position ledger even though the official Registry provides declarant reconciliation views.

contrary_evidence: The official CBAM Registry's DRMC component already shows imported goods, emissions, certificates, and penalties, creating direct functional overlap: https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/cbam-registry_en

Accredited verification and Registry workflows may cause customers to buy bundled services from established customs and assurance firms: https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/cbam-verification_en

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with one customs representative or verifier to reconstruct a 2026 portfolio, then convert affected importers to recurring position management.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 8 importers at PLN 7,000 MRR in year 2, 30 at PLN 10,000 MRR in year 4, and 50 at PLN 12,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 7.2m ARR before line fees. At 25% owner earnings or a 3-4x ARR value and 60% ownership, PLN 5m net worth is plausible in years 5-7; if the official DRMC fully replaces internal reconciliation for pilots, stop.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day for one sector and customs format; use accredited partners and remain outside formal verification.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 75-88% for software; emissions consulting and accredited verification are partner services, not included labor.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: improved certificate cash forecasting and fewer unsupported lines repay the annual fee; validate with a shadow liability close.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 3,000-15,000 monthly per importer plus PLN 5-30 per import line and paid historical reconstruction.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Imports, certificate prices, evidence updates, and Registry reconciliation recur; supplier-installation mapping is difficult to recreate.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: supplier-installation evidence maps and line-classification history reduce repeated collection work; forecast accuracy improves with each quarter
fingerprint.customer: EU midmarket importers and indirect customs representatives handling cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, or hydrogen above the mass threshold
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: customs agencies, ERP trade-compliance partners, accredited verifiers, and a fixed-fee 2026 liability reconstruction
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: customs-line ingestion, supplier evidence requests, emissions and foreign-carbon-price provenance, certificate exposure forecast, Registry reconciliation, and auditor export; subscription plus line volume
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: importer or customs representative pays per portfolio month and import line when forecast exposure and Registry actuals are reconciled
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a shipment, quarter close, certificate purchase, or annual declaration changes the expected carbon liability and finance needs a defensible position

founder_fit: Carbon-liability modeling and evidence reconciliation align with data science and finance interests.
A single-sector Polish importer wedge is buildable part-time with partner expertise.
The service can validate on historical data before major spending.
Customs and verifier channels reduce dependence on broad networking or a public persona.
risks: The CBAM Registry already includes a data-reconciliation component.
Incorrect liability forecasts can have material financial consequences.
Formal verification is reserved for accredited verifiers; positioning must be precise.
Regulatory simplification, thresholds, default values, and covered products can change.

structure.control_point: forecast-to-actual CBAM certificate exposure by import line before purchase, declaration, and surrender
structure.critical_dependency: complete customs data and installation-level embedded-emissions evidence that can be linked to accredited verification and Registry records

thesis: For EU importers just above the CBAM threshold, maintain an internal liability position that joins customs lines, supplier installations, embedded-emissions evidence, verified reports, carbon price paid abroad, quarterly certificate prices, registry balances, and annual surrender. The official Registry and accredited verifier remain authoritative. The wedge is treasury-grade forecast-to-actual reconciliation across procurement, customs, sustainability, and finance, paid per portfolio month and import line.
title: CBAM Import-Line Liability and Certificate Position Ledger
uncertainties: It is unknown whether midmarket importers need a separate ledger beyond broker, ERP, and Registry tools.
Access to clean customs and supplier-installation data is untested.
The most attractive first CBAM sector and buyer are uncertain.
Certificate-price exposure and willingness to pay have not been quantified per customer.
